## Reading

Loukissas, Chapter 6, _Models of Local Practice_, pp. 161–188. [Session 8](08-models-of-local-practice-i.qmd) reads the same chapter from a different angle.

## Reading summary

The chapter proposes six practical moves:

1. Look at the data setting.
2. Make place part of data presentation.
3. Compare data instead of treating them as uniform.
4. Challenge normative algorithms with counterdata.
5. Create interfaces that introduce useful friction.
6. Use data to build relationships.

Design can support critical reflection by making hidden attachments, values, absences, and biases easier to inspect.

## In class

Students apply at least two of these moves to the dataset they brought to class.

## Output

A written application of at least two moves to your own dataset.
